lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: No one would have believed it, in those last years of the century. Our world was being watched.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Across the gulf of space, minds vast and cool watched our green Earth with envy.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then Lavelle of Java wired news of a huge flame bursting out of Mars.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Men went about their little affairs. I was busy writing essays on moral progress.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I might never have heard of it, but for Ogilvy, the astronomer at Ottershaw. He was wild.

lines.speaker: ogilvy
lines.text: Come and look. It came out of Mars like a shot from a gun.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I remember that vigil: the black dome, the lantern low, the clockwork ticking.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Through the glass: deep blue, and in the middle of it the little planet, swimming.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: So small, so bright. Forty million miles of darkness lay between us.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Ogilvy moved about in the dark behind me, as the chronometer ran toward midnight.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Ogilvy! A red flash, just now, at the edge of it!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He took the eyepiece at once, and cried out at the plume of gas.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I felt my way to the siphon, green and crimson swimming before my eyes.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I never dreamed of it. That night a second missile left Mars, flying for us.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At one o'clock he gave up the watch, and we lit the lantern.

lines.speaker: ogilvy
lines.text: The chances against anything manlike on Mars are a million to one.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We walked down to his house. Below us, Ottershaw and Chertsey slept in peace.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: For ten nights the flames came, and the papers joked about volcanoes on Mars.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: One warm night, I took my wife out walking under the stars.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I showed her the Zodiac, and Mars creeping overhead.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Lights burned in upper windows. Far off, trains rang, soft as music.

lines.speaker: narrators_wife
lines.text: Look, dear, the signal lights. Red and green and yellow. So bright.
